correctness.rationale: For modulo-three walk increments iid, B_t=1{Y_t neq 0} are iid Bernoulli(2/3) under both iid-null and cyclic alternative. The observed-count plug-in runs center deviates from 2n/3 by O_P(1) and variance is 2n/9+o_P(n). Nontrivial Markov eigenvalues are +/-i sqrt(3) delta, giving the positive covariance factor (1-3delta^2)/(1+3delta^2). Standard finite-chain additive CLT gives scaled chi-square_2, and exact chi-square_2 tail with union bound yields limsup power below alpha. The direction score has nonzero LLN mean. A standalone exact-rational checker passed 68 assertions on n=2,...,8; finite work is corroboration rather than proof.

value.rationale: The result identifies a precise and surprising statistical blind spot: a plausible published independence assessment has an asymptotic rejection bound strictly below nominal size on a nontrivially dependent, uniform-marginal process, even though a one-dimensional directional transition contrast is consistent. It gives a complete analytic parameter family and an explicit decision-theoretic boundary, not a routine single numerical example.
